data.message: Starting cyber investigation with host-authorized tools.

Live browsing of https://malware.wicar.org redirected to https://www.wicar.org/test-malware.html (HTTP 200), which presents a menu of named anti-malware test payloads (EICAR, CVE-2014-6332, CVE-2012-4681, JS crypto miner) with a user disclaimer. Common Crawl shows the host archived across 2021-2026 with /data/ test pages. No exploit or download link was activated.

report.summary:
Verdict: no malicious behavior observed (deliberate, self-identified anti-malware test site). Confidence: medium-high.

Live isolated browsing of https://malware.wicar.org (host scope, desktop profile) returned HTTP 200 and the page immediately navigated to https://www.wicar.org/test-malware.html, titled "Test Malware! - WICAR.org - Test Your Anti-Malware Solution!". The rendered page and screenshot show a catalogue of clearly labelled, opt-in test payloads (EICAR test file, CVE-2014-6332 MS14-064, CVE-2012-4681 Java 7 applet, MS03-020, MS05-054, MS09-002, MS09-072, MS10-090, Firefox exposedProps CVE-2012-3993, VLC AMV CVE-2010-3275, Adobe Flash CVE-2015-5119, and a JavaScript crypto miner), each in HTTP and SSL variants under malware.wicar.org/data/, plus instructions that "Ideally, all tests should be blocked by your anti-malware defences" and a liability disclaimer. Nothing was auto-served on load: only the two document requests were recorded, with no drive-by script, redirect chain to third-party infrastructure, or automatic download.

Common Crawl historical evidence (2021-2026, crawls CC-MAIN-2021-43 through CC-MAIN-2026-39) shows the same structure has been publicly archived for years; the 2025-01-23 root capture is only a 301 redirect, consistent with the live redirect to www.wicar.org. The site's stated purpose is security-control testing, but it does host real exploit and miner content behind user-initiated links; that content was not activated or executed in this assessment, so its current live payloads remain untested.
uncertainties: No /data/ exploit page, EICAR file, or crypto-miner script was fetched or executed, so current live payload behaviour, hashes and any post-2026 content changes are untested.

The DOM section for the initial view was not captured (dom_capture:Error) and the follow-on page capture was reported truncated with network_requests_failed, so sub-resource and script-level evidence for the landing page is incomplete.
No forms, scripts or frames sections were inspected, and no mobile-profile session was run, so profile-dependent or script-triggered behaviour is unobserved.
Common Crawl results are sampled partitions (at most 30 captures, no 2022 capture returned) and represent historical, not current, site state; archive presence or absence does not establish safety.

No passive DNS, WHOIS, TLS certificate, reputation or threat-intelligence enrichment was authorized or performed, so domain ownership and hosting infrastructure are unverified; absence of detections is not proof of safety.
recommendations: Treat malware.wicar.org as intentional test content: allow it only from isolated, instrumented test hosts and keep it blocked on production endpoints and user networks.
If validating controls, expect EICAR and the listed CVE test pages to be blocked; an unblocked blank page indicates the control did not detect the test, per the site's own guidance.
Do not fetch or execute /data/ resources (eicar.com, exploit HTML, js_crypto_miner.html) outside a disposable sandbox; the JavaScript miner is advertised as consuming significant CPU.
If an endpoint alert cites this domain, correlate with whether a sanctioned test was in progress before treating it as a real compromise.

findings.statement: Live browsing of the submitted URL returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://www.wicar.org/test-malware.html; only two document requests were recorded (malware.wicar.org/ and www.wicar.org/test-malware.html) with no automatic third-party resource loads, scripted drive-by activity, or unprompted download on page load.

The live landing page self-identifies as WICAR.org, an anti-malware test harness: it instructs users to select a test payload, states all tests should ideally be blocked by their defences, and carries a liability disclaimer. Captured page text and the screenshot list named CVE-labelled test items (EICAR, CVE-2014-6332, CVE-2012-4681, CVE-2003-0344, CVE-2005-1790, CVE-2009-0075, CVE-2009-3672, CVE-2010-3962, CVE-2012-3993, CVE-2010-3275, CVE-2015-5119) and a JavaScript cryptocurrency miner, each as HTTP and SSL links under malware.wicar.org/data/. This indicates deliberate, consent-based security testing rather than covert malicious delivery.

Historical Common Crawl evidence corroborates long-standing, stable test-site structure: captures of malware.wicar.org exist from 2021-10-25 through 2026-09-10 across crawls CC-MAIN-2021-43 to CC-MAIN-2026-39, including /data/ exploit-test pages (ms03_020_ie_objecttype.html, ms05_054_onload.html, ms09_002_memory_corruption.html, ms14_064_ole_xp.html, java_jre17_exec.html, vlc_amv.html, js_crypto_miner.html). The archived root capture of 2025-01-23 contains only a 301 Moved Permanently response, matching the live redirect behaviour, and the archived js_crypto_miner.html capture of 2026-01-13 returned HTTP 200 with effectively empty extracted text.

Although the intent is testing, the host advertises genuine exploit code and a CPU-consuming crypto miner reachable one click away, so the domain should still be treated as hostile content in production environments. Per instructions no exploit/test link or download was activated, and the DOM section for the initial view was unavailable (dom_capture error), so the actual payload behaviour of /data/ resources is unverified in this assessment. The session was closed cleanly (cleanup_status stopped).
